details.description: Mistral Small 4 (API id mistral-small-2603) is an open-weight model Mistral AI released on March 16, 2026 that it describes as consolidating the strengths of three previously separate models -- Magistral's reasoning, Devstral's agentic coding, and Mistral Small's instruction-following -- into one hybrid model. It is a mixture-of-experts model with 128 experts (4 active per token), 119B total parameters (6B active per token, 8B including embedding and output layers), a 256k-token context window, and text-plus-image input. A configurable reasoning-effort setting lets the same model give fast, low-effort answers or deeper, higher-effort reasoning on a per-request basis. It is released under the Apache 2.0 license with open weights.
advantages: Mistral AI reports a 40% reduction in end-to-end completion latency and 3x more requests per second versus Mistral Small 3 in latency- and throughput-optimized deployment setups.
Mistral AI reports the model outperforms GPT-OSS 120B on LiveCodeBench while producing 20% less output.

Supports a reasoning_effort parameter that trades off between fast, low-effort responses (comparable to Mistral Small 3.2) and deep, high-effort reasoning (matching prior Magistral verbosity) within a single model.
Released with open weights under the Apache 2.0 license, available via Hugging Face and NVIDIA NIM in addition to Mistral's own API.
use_cases: Agentic coding tasks such as multi-step code generation and editing
Complex reasoning tasks with an adjustable reasoning-effort level
Document analysis and visual understanding via image input

notes: Mistral's own models-overview documentation lists mistral-small-2603 as the current API id for 'Mistral Small 4' (v26.03, Apache 2.0), matching the catalog's canonical name; the catalog's 262144-token input/output limits and image+text modality match the maker's stated 256k context window and multimodal input. The launch post gives an AA-LCR score of '0.72' for this model but never states whether that is a 0-1 fraction or a percentage, so it is left out of evaluations rather than converted to 72.0; no other numeric benchmark for this exact model (as opposed to relative claims like 'outperforms GPT-OSS 120B') was found on the maker's page. The maker states the model has 'multilingual support' but names no specific languages, so languages is left empty.
